sketchMechanisms: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance, forever. Combined with `companion object`, it exists only inside another class, never independently.
Rust's ownership system means passing a value to a function moves it — the caller can no longer use it. The variable is consumed and inaccessible after the call.
A LEFT JOIN preserves every row from the left table even when no matching row exists on the right — the result fills with NULLs where the other side is absent.
